observations.text: SP established two-way communication with the ground station only after the IP had passed the initial contact call on the first two frequencies, and the R/T panel selections were made as directed from the front cockpit. Radio procedures were executed correctly once each call was dictated, but no transmission was initiated from SP's own assessment of the phase of flight. Performance is at the code desired for this Training Section but marginal, as the R/T was worked to instruction rather than to procedure. Self-initiated initial contact after each frequency change is expected in the following sorties.

SP operated the R/T from engine start to engine shut down, selecting the frequencies and transmitting without the IP taking over any call, requiring the IP's verbal prompt to begin the initial contact on two occasions. One instruction from the ground station was read back incorrectly and was corrected with delay, after the IP pointed out the difference. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP established two-way communication with the ground station and with the other A/C in the area without any support from the IP, and executed the initial contact after each frequency change. Minor errors of phraseology on two calls were recognized by SP and re-transmitted in the standard format in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention, and all instructions received were followed without misinterpretation. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP handled the R/T throughout the mission with standard phraseology on every call, obtaining contact with the ground station and the other A/C without support from the IP. Calls addressed to the A/C were answered as soon as they were received, no transmission was made over another station after a frequency change, and every instruction was read back correctly and complied with. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP operated the R/T from engine start to engine shut down with continuous monitoring of both the tower and the area frequency, answering every call directed to the A/C on first transmission. Phraseology was standard on all calls, initial contact was executed at each frequency change without ever transmitting over an exchange already in progress, and instructions were read back and complied with without a single request for repetition. The accuracy and the speed of the R/T work exceed the levels expected of a student at this stage of the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an unrehearsed call format that was composed on the frequency rather than before transmitting, could not establish two-way communication with the ground station after the departure frequency change. Three attempts were transmitted with the call sign and the position of the A/C omitted, and the IP took the R/T and executed the initial contact. The remaining frequency changes were directed by the IP call by call. Study of the standard R/T formats for each phase of the mission is required before the next sortie.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not monitor the ground station frequency during the transition to the flight area and left two calls addressed to the A/C unanswered. The IP answered both calls and thereafter directed the frequency selections and the content of each transmission. The R/T could not be worked without assistance for the remainder of the sortie.

SP worked the R/T at the desired standard for this Training Section, establishing two-way communication with the ground station after the IP's verbal prompt at each of the three frequency changes. One instruction from the tower was misread and was corrected with delay once the IP repeated it, and no call was left unanswered after prompting. Marginal performance for the Training Section - initial contact executed without prompting, from SP's own tracking of the phase of flight, is expected in the following sorties.

SP established two-way communication with the ground station and with the other A/C without support from the IP and executed the initial contact after each frequency change. Two calls were made with non-standard phraseology, both recognized by SP and immediately re-transmitted in the correct format without the IP's intervention. The instructions received from the ground station were followed without misinterpretation. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP monitored the assigned frequencies continuously from engine start to engine shut down and responded to every call from the ground station and from the other A/C as soon as it was received. Contact was obtained with the standard procedures and phraseology on each occasion, no exchange between the ground station and another A/C was interrupted, and every instruction was read back correctly and precisely followed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated complete command of the operation and use of the R/T, selecting and checking each frequency ahead of the phase of flight that required it and executing initial contact without a single prompt from the IP. Every call directed to the A/C was answered on first transmission, all phraseology was standard, and the instructions from the ground station were complied with without any request for repetition or clarification. The precision and the speed of the R/T work are above the levels expected at this stage of the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an R/T panel worked without the next frequency preselected, lost two-way communication with the ground station after the departure frequency change and did not recover it on the alternative selection. The IP had to select the correct frequency and execute the initial contact, and thereafter passed the calls for the remainder of the recovery. The requirement to establish two-way communication with the ground station was not met without assistance.

SP, due to transmission over another station, so that the reply was masked, did not obtain contact with the tower after the frequency change and repeated the same blocked call twice. The IP intervened, directed SP to wait for the exchange in progress to finish and passed the initial contact call. The instructions already issued to the A/C were not received and had to be relayed by the IP.

SP, due to a call format built without the required elements, transmitted the initial contact after the frequency change without the position and the intentions of the A/C. The ground station requested the missing information twice, and the complete call was made only after the IP's verbal prompt. The omission was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during a critical phase of flight, did not continuously monitor the ground station frequency and left two calls addressed to the A/C unanswered. Both were answered only after the IP's verbal prompt, and the second instruction was read back with delay. The IP took no control of the R/T, but the calls were not responded to as soon as possible.

SP worked the R/T within the desired standards, establishing two-way communication with the ground station and the other A/C without support from the IP and executing initial contact at each frequency change. Two transmissions departed from the standard phraseology and were re-worded by SP in a timely manner without the IP's intervention, and one call on the area frequency was answered late while the maneuver was being flown. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a standard call format on first transmission and continuous monitoring of both frequencies during maneuvering are expected to improve.

SP monitored the tower and the area frequencies throughout the mission and answered every call addressed to the A/C as soon as it was received. Contact was obtained with the ground station and with the other A/C following the standard procedures and phraseology on every occasion, no communication in progress was interrupted after a frequency change, and all instructions were read back correctly and precisely followed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP managed the R/T from engine start to engine shut down with the next frequency preselected before each phase of the mission and initial contact executed without a single prompt from the IP. Every call was made in standard phraseology and answered on first transmission, no exchange between the ground station and another A/C was blocked, and no instruction required repetition or clarification. The R/T work was accomplished with an accuracy and a speed above the levels expected of a student in this Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an R/T sequence in which the frequency was changed before the current instruction had been read back, lost the exchange with the tower during the recovery and could not re-establish two-way communication with either station. The IP took the R/T, re-selected the previous frequency and completed the read-back and the initial contact on the new frequency. The remaining calls of the recovery were directed by the IP. The R/T procedures applicable to a frequency change are to be reviewed before the next sortie.

SP, due to an unstated request for a repeat of the instruction that was not understood, read back a runway assignment that had not been issued by the tower and began to comply with it. The IP intervened, stopped the action, obtained the correct instruction and completed the exchange with the ground station. The instruction was misinterpreted and the correction was not achieved without the IP executing part of the communication.

SP, due to a listening watch maintained on one frequency only while both were required, did not respond to two calls from the other A/C in the area. Both calls were answered after the IP's verbal prompt, and the position report requested was passed with delay. Communication with the ground station was maintained throughout, but the calls were not responded to as soon as possible.

SP, due to failure to pass a required call at the briefed point, did not report entering the flight area to the ground station and did not execute the initial contact after the frequency change. The call was made only after the IP's verbal prompt and the omission was recognized with delay. The standard procedures and phraseology were correct once the transmission was made, and no instruction was misinterpreted.

SP, due to a call composed while the A/C was being maneuvered rather than before the transmission, made the initial contact after the frequency change with the elements of the call sign and the position transmitted out of the standard order. The error was recognized by SP and the call was immediately repeated in the correct format, without the IP's intervention. Two-way communication with the ground station and with the other A/C was maintained for the remainder of the mission and all instructions were followed without misinterpretation.

SP, due to stress associated with the check-ride environment, transmitted the initial contact on the area frequency before the exchange between the ground station and the preceding A/C had finished. SP recognized that the call had been blocked, waited and re-transmitted in a timely manner without the IP's intervention, and contact was then obtained with the standard phraseology. No instruction was missed and the error had no effect on the conduct of the mission.

SP worked the R/T at the desired standard for this Training Section, obtaining contact with the ground station and the other A/C with the standard procedures and phraseology and following every instruction without misinterpretation. Two calls addressed to the A/C during the maneuvering phase were answered after a noticeable pause, and one read-back was completed more slowly than the traffic on the frequency allowed. Marginal performance for the Training Section - the accuracy already shown is to be maintained while the speed of response under maneuvering workload is expected to improve.

SP operated the R/T from engine start to engine shut down with every frequency preselected ahead of the phase of the mission that required it, and executed the initial contact on each change without any prompt from the IP. All calls were made in standard phraseology and answered on first transmission, no exchange in progress was ever blocked, and each instruction from the ground station was read back correctly and complied with immediately. Continuous monitoring of both frequencies was maintained through the working phase, with the responses to the other A/C passed without any interruption of the maneuver being flown. Above end of block MIF achieved.
